literal: When the Six Offices were established, he was dismissed from Left Palace Steward.
idiomatic: When the Six Offices were set up, he was removed as Left Palace Steward.

literal: When Emperor Xiaomin took the throne, he went out as Inspector of Weizhou.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xiaomin ascended, Yi was sent out as Inspector of Weizhou.

literal: Yi's elder brother Shi had earlier come to this province and had quite benevolent government.
idiomatic: Yi's elder brother Shi had governed the province before him and left a record of kindness.

literal: Yi again extended sincerity and spread trust; affairs were kept lenient and simple; barbarians and Chinese alike were moved and pleased, comparing him to the greater and lesser Lords Feng.
idiomatic: Yi in turn ruled with sincerity and trust, keeping government lenient and spare. Barbarian and Chinese alike rejoiced, likening him to the greater and lesser Lords Feng.

literal: At the time Tuyuhun invaded the right of the Yellow River; Liang, Shan, and He provinces were all besieged, and envoys came reporting urgency.
idiomatic: Tuyuhun then raided the west bank of the Yellow River. Liang, Shan, and He were all under siege, and urgent dispatches arrived.

literal: The Area Commander of Qinzhou sent Yi to go to the rescue; he would not follow, and all the staff spoke against it.
idiomatic: The Area Commander of Qinzhou ordered Yi to relieve them. He refused, and every member of his staff remonstrated.

literal: Yi said: "The arts of storming and taking are not what barbarian custom excels at.
idiomatic: Yi said, "Storming walled places is not what these tribes do best.

literal: This band's coming is nothing beyond raiding the border pastures—how could they mass troops below the walls and long pursue siege!
idiomatic: This raid is only border plunder. How could they camp under our walls and sit in a long siege?

literal: If they raid and gain nothing, the momentum will make them withdraw on their own.
idiomatic: Raid without booty, and they will withdraw of themselves.

literal: To weary the army going there would also accomplish nothing.
idiomatic: To weary our troops marching there would gain us nothing.

literal: Yi had already gauged this to the end—pray do not speak again."
idiomatic: I have already read this through to the end—please say no more."

literal: Several days later inquiries arrived, and it was indeed as Yi had strategized.
idiomatic: Within days the reports came in, exactly as Yi had predicted.

literal: Helan Xiang attacked Tuyuhun; Yi led the province's troops as vanguard in deep penetration and, for merit, had his fief increased.
idiomatic: When Helan Xiang campaigned against Tuyuhun, Yi led provincial troops as vanguard deep into enemy country and, for merit, received an enlarged fief.

literal: Soon he was summoned and appointed Right Palace Steward.
idiomatic: He was soon recalled and made Right Palace Steward.

literal: Emperor Ming greatly loved literature and history; he established the Linqi Academy, and among those at court with artistic accomplishment, without limit of noble or base, all were permitted to join.
idiomatic: Emperor Ming loved letters and history. He founded the Linqi Academy, and every courtier with learning, noble or humble, might attend.

literal: Thus even Xiao Kou, Wang Bao, and others were together scholars with base-born fellows.
idiomatic: Thus Xiao Kou, Wang Bao, and others sat as fellows beside men of low birth.

literal: Yi spoke to the emperor, saying: "Kou is a clansman of Liang;
idiomatic: Yi told the emperor, "Kou is a prince of Liang;

literal: Bao is a grandee of Liang—now to mount the same steps with runners in attendance, I fear this is not the meaning of honoring the worthy and prizing rank."
idiomatic: Bao is a Liang grandee. To share the runners' stair with them is hardly honoring worth and rank."

literal: The emperor accepted it; an edict ordered Yi to fix their class order, and thereby there were gradations.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed and ordered Yi to set their seating order, and gradations were established.

literal: When Emperor Ming died, Yi together with Duke of Jin Hu received the testamentary edict and installed Emperor Wu.
idiomatic: When Emperor Ming died, Yi and Duke of Jin Hu received the deathbed edict and enthroned Emperor Wu.

literal: In the first year of Baoding he was transferred to Army Marshal.
idiomatic: In Baoding year one he became Army Marshal.

literal: In the third year he was enfeoffed Duke of Changshan commandery.
idiomatic: In year three he was enfeoffed Duke of Changshan commandery.

literal: At the beginning of Tianhe he was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Accounts, Grand Master.
idiomatic: At the opening of Tianhe he was promoted to Director of the Bureau of Accounts, Grand Master.

literal: In the third year the empress of the Ashina clan arrived from the Turks; Emperor Wu performed the ceremony of greeting her in person and ordered Yi to oversee all ritual observances.
idiomatic: In year three the Ashina empress arrived from the Turks. Emperor Wu went out to greet her in person and put Yi in charge of all court ritual.

literal: Though the Di people squatted without decorum, all feared Yi's ritual law and none dared violate it.
idiomatic: Though the Di still squatted without ceremony, they all feared Yi's ritual discipline and dared not break it.

literal: He met his father's death and left office; in mourning he exceeded the rites, and his contemporaries praised him.
idiomatic: On his father's death he left office and mourned beyond the prescribed rites, to the praise of his peers.

literal: Soon an edict recalled him and ordered him to resume duties.
idiomatic: Soon an edict recalled him to duty.

literal: Emperor Wu also, because Yi had discernment in human relations, entrusted to Yi the selection and placement of the crown prince, all the princes, and those who instructed them and below.
idiomatic: The emperor also, trusting Yi's eye for men, entrusted him with choosing tutors and attendants for the crown prince and every prince.

literal: Those he raised and employed were all men of popular repute; opinion at the time unanimously said he had found the right men.
idiomatic: Every man he advanced enjoyed public renown, and contemporaries agreed he had chosen well.

literal: He was promoted Grand General and oversaw all inner and outer palace-guard military affairs.
idiomatic: He was made Grand General and commanded all palace guards within and without.

literal: Duke of Jin Hu, because the emperor entrusted Yi as his intimate, harbored suspicion inwardly; he transferred him to Junior Minister of Education and additionally appointed him Pillar of State.
idiomatic: Duke of Jin Hu, seeing the emperor trust Yi as his intimate, grew jealous inwardly. Yi was shifted to Junior Minister of Education with the added title Pillar of State.

literal: Though outwardly showing lofty honor, in fact he was pushed aside.
idiomatic: Outwardly he was honored; in truth he was pushed aside.

literal: When Hu was executed, the emperor summoned Yi and sent him to Hedong to take Hu's son Duke of Zhongshan Xun, and he still replaced him in garrisoning Pu Prefecture.
idiomatic: When Hu was killed, the emperor summoned Yi, sent him to Hedong to seize Hu's son Duke of Zhongshan Xun, and left him to hold Pu Prefecture.

literal: Yi said: "The Chancellor lacked a lord and overawed his sovereign, and brought execution on himself.
idiomatic: Yi said, "The Chancellor lorded it over his sovereign and earned his own destruction.

literal: Once the chief evil is removed, the remaining spawn ought to be exterminated.
idiomatic: The chief villain is gone; the remnant brood should be wiped out.

literal: Yet they are all Your Majesty's flesh and blood, and one still says the distant do not come between the near.
idiomatic: Yet they are Your Majesty's own kin, and it is said the distant must not come between the near.

literal: If Your Majesty does not send one of the princes but sends me, a man of another surname, it is not only that the world will have sideways talk—this foolish minister also has not found peace."
idiomatic: If Your Majesty sends not a prince but me, a man of another surname, the world will murmur—and I myself will not be at ease."

literal: The emperor agreed and thereupon sent Prince of Yue Sheng to replace Yi.
idiomatic: The emperor agreed and sent Prince of Yue Sheng in Yi's place.

literal: Earlier, with Qi and Chen on the two borders, each repaired frontier defenses; though envoys passed with friendly missions, every year there was fighting.
idiomatic: Earlier, along the Qi and Chen frontiers each side had strengthened its defenses. Envoys still came with courtesies, yet every year brought battle.

literal: Yet first here, then there, neither could achieve capture or gain.
idiomatic: Victory shifted from side to side, yet neither could win a lasting gain.

literal: After Emperor Wu personally handled the myriad affairs, he was about to plan an eastern campaign; he ordered the border towns and garrisons all to increase stored grain and add garrison troops.
idiomatic: Once Emperor Wu took the reins himself and planned an eastern campaign, he ordered every border town to stock more grain and add garrison troops.

literal: The two states heard of it and also increased repair of defenses.
idiomatic: Qi and Chen heard of it and strengthened their defenses in turn.

literal: Yi remonstrated, saying: "On the frontier they invade one another, each having victory and defeat—only soldiers and stores are wasted; this is not the highest policy.
idiomatic: Yi remonstrated: "Border raids trade victories and defeats, but only waste men and grain. That is not the best policy.

literal: Better to relax the border alert, reduce troops on defense, renew friendship and let the people rest, and respectfully await those who come.
idiomatic: Better to ease the frontier, cut garrisons, renew friendship, let the people rest, and receive arrivals with courtesy.

literal: They will surely delight in communication and peace, slacken and be without defense—then strike from beyond their expectation, and in one move the east of the mountains can be taken."
idiomatic: They will rejoice in peace, grow slack and unready—then strike where they do not expect, and the east of the mountains may be taken at a stroke."

literal: The emperor accepted it.
idiomatic: The emperor accepted his advice.

literal: In the second year of Jiande he went out as Area Commander of Anzhou.
idiomatic: In Jiande year two he went out as Area Commander of Anzhou.

literal: At the time there was great drought; the Yu River ceased to flow.
idiomatic: A great drought struck; the Yu River ran dry.

literal: By old custom, whenever there was severe drought, they prayed at Mount Baizhao for rain.
idiomatic: By old custom, in severe drought the people prayed for rain at Mount Baizhao.

literal: The emperor had earlier forbidden mass sacrifices; the mountain shrine had already been removed.
idiomatic: The emperor had forbidden mass sacrifices, and the mountain shrine had been torn down.

literal: Yi sent the chief clerk to sacrifice there, and that very day a timely rain fell.
idiomatic: Yi sent his chief clerk to sacrifice there, and that very day a soaking rain fell.

literal: The year thereby had a harvest.
idiomatic: The year brought a harvest.

literal: The common people were moved by it; they gathered, sang and danced, and praised him.
idiomatic: The people were moved. They gathered, sang, danced, and praised him.

literal: In the fourth year Emperor Wu was about to campaign east; the court ministers did not yet know.
idiomatic: In year four the emperor planned an eastern campaign, unknown to the court.

literal: He sent Censor Lu Yun, three times by relay post, to go to Yi and ask his strategy.
idiomatic: He sent Censor Lu Yun by relay post, three times in succession, to ask Yi's counsel.

literal: Yi endorsed and supported it.
idiomatic: Yi endorsed the plan.

literal: When the army marched out, an edict ordered Yi from Wan and Ye to hurry to Xiangcheng; in ten days he took nineteen Qi cities.
idiomatic: When the army marched, Yi was ordered from Wan and Ye toward Xiangcheng. In ten days he took nineteen Qi cities.

literal: Where he passed, not a hair was violated.
idiomatic: Where he passed, not a hair was harmed.

literal: If any commander under him entered a village of people, he was immediately beheaded to warn the host.
idiomatic: Any subordinate commander who entered a civilian village was beheaded on the spot as a warning.

literal: Thereby the common people were glad and pleased; those who came went as to their home.
idiomatic: The people rejoiced and came to him as to their own home.

literal: Because the emperor fell ill, the army withdrew; Yi also returned to his command.
idiomatic: The emperor fell ill and withdrew the army; Yi too returned to his post.

literal: He was transferred to Area Commander of Yiyang.
idiomatic: He was transferred to Area Commander of Yiyang.

literal: Because Yiyang's terrain was not a strategic throat, he requested moving the command to Shan.
idiomatic: Yiyang was no strategic choke point; he asked to move headquarters to Shan.

literal: The edict followed him; he was still made Inspector of Shan Prefecture, Area Commander as before.
idiomatic: The edict granted it. He was made Inspector of Shan while keeping the area command.

literal: That year the great army again campaigned east; Yi entered from Shan and went straight to Luoyang.
idiomatic: That year the main army campaigned east again. Yi entered from Shan and went straight to Luoyang.

literal: Qi Governor of Luoyang Dugu Chengye opened the gates and surrendered; the nine provinces and thirty garrisons of Henan all fell at once.
idiomatic: Qi's Governor of Luoyang Dugu Chengye opened the gates and surrendered. Nine provinces and thirty Henan garrisons fell at once.

literal: The people of Xiangcheng and so on were glad to see Yi again and all set out pots of drink by the road to welcome him.
idiomatic: The people of Xiangcheng rejoiced to see Yi again and lined the road with pots of drink.

literal: He was appointed Area Commander of Heyang and still transferred to Yuzhou.
idiomatic: He was made Area Commander of Heyang, then transferred to Yuzhou.

literal: Chen general Lu Tiannian had long besieged Guang Prefecture; hearing Yi had reached Runan, he scattered before the wind and withdrew.
idiomatic: Chen general Lu Tiannian had long besieged Guang Prefecture. When he heard Yi had reached Runan, he broke camp and fled.

literal: At the beginning of Daxiang he was summoned and appointed Grand Minister of Education.
idiomatic: At the opening of Daxiang he was recalled and made Grand Minister of Education.

literal: An edict ordered Yi to tour the Long Wall and establish beacon towers and border posts.
idiomatic: An edict ordered Yi to tour the Long Wall and set up beacon towers and border posts.

literal: From Yanmen in the west to Jieshi in the east, whether newly built or old and altered, all obtained their strategic points.
idiomatic: From Yanmen in the west to Jieshi in the east, whether newly built or old and refitted, every post sat on a key point.

literal: He was still made Area Commander of Youzhou.
idiomatic: He was also made Area Commander of Youzhou.

literal: Earlier the Turks had repeatedly raided and plundered; the inhabitants lost their livelihoods.
idiomatic: Earlier the Turks had raided again and again, and the people lost their livelihood.

literal: Yi had long possessed martial awe and was also skilled in reconnaissance; from then on they did not dare violate the frontier passes, and the common people were secure.
idiomatic: Yi had long held martial awe and knew reconnaissance. From then on they dared not cross the passes, and the people lived in peace.

literal: When Yuchi Jiong held Xiang Prefecture and raised troops, he sent a letter to recruit Yi.
idiomatic: When Yuchi Jiong seized Xiang Prefecture and rebelled, he wrote to win Yi over.

literal: Yi seized his envoy and, together with the letter, sent them on.
idiomatic: Yi seized the envoy and forwarded him with the letter.

literal: At the time Emperor Wen of Sui held the government; he bestowed on Yi fifteen hundred lengths of mixed silks, together with treasures, robes, and playthings.
idiomatic: Yang Jian then held power. He gave Yi fifteen hundred lengths of mixed silk, with treasures, robes, and fine objects.

literal: He was advanced to Senior Pillar of State, enfeoffed Duke of Ren state, with fief households totaling five thousand together with earlier grants; separately he received the tax revenue of Rencheng county, one thousand households.
idiomatic: He was advanced to Senior Pillar of State and enfeoffed Duke of Ren, five thousand households in all with earlier grants. He separately received the tax of Rencheng county, one thousand households.

literal: Yi also sent his son Rang with a memorial urging accession and also requested to enter court; this was granted.
idiomatic: Yi also sent his son Rang with a memorial urging Yang Jian to take the throne and asked leave to come to court; both were granted.

literal: At the beginning of Sui's Kaihuang, Yi entered court; the emperor descended from the couch, took his hand, and was exceedingly glad.
idiomatic: At the opening of Kaihuang, Yi came to court. The emperor stepped down from the couch, took his hand, and rejoiced exceedingly.

literal: Several days later he was appointed Grand Commandant.
idiomatic: Within days he was made Grand Commandant.

literal: Someone reported that Yi, when formerly in Youzhou, had wished to join Yuchi Jiong.
idiomatic: Someone reported that Yi, while in Youzhou, had meant to join Yuchi Jiong.

literal: On investigation there was no fact; he was forgiven.
idiomatic: Investigation found no truth in it, and he was forgiven.

literal: In the third year he died in his original post.
idiomatic: In year three he died in office.

literal: Posthumously he was given Commander over the armies of six provinces and Inspector of Pu Prefecture; posthumous name Mu.
idiomatic: Posthumously he was made commander over six provinces' armies and Inspector of Pu, with posthumous name Mu.

literal: Yi's nature was respectful and frugal; he contended with nothing; he constantly took fullness as a warning to himself—therefore he could end with merit and fame.
idiomatic: Yi was respectful and frugal and contended with no one. He constantly warned himself against fullness, and so ended his days in merit and fame.

literal: His son Xi succeeded.
idiomatic: His son Xi succeeded.

literal: Xi, styled Bofu, in youth had capacity and ability.
idiomatic: Xi, styled Bofu, showed talent and resolve early.

literal: He served Zhou as Director of the Masters of Equipage, Grand Master, and was enfeoffed Duke of Liyang county.
idiomatic: Under Zhou he was Director of the Masters of Equipage, Grand Master, and Duke of Liyang county.

literal: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he was transferred to Director of the Right Merit Bureau, Grand Master.
idiomatic: When Emperor Xuan succeeded, he became Director of the Right Merit Bureau, Grand Master.

literal: Soon he also led the Right Righteousness Guard.
idiomatic: Soon he also commanded the Right Righteousness Guard.

literal: When Emperor Wen of Sui received the abdication, he was given the additional title Grand General and advanced in rank to Duke of a commandery.
idiomatic: When Emperor Wen took the throne, Xi was made Grand General and advanced to a commandery duke.

literal: He successively served as Inspector of Bian and Shao, and in every post he had kindness and favor.
idiomatic: He served as Inspector of Bian and Shao in turn, and in each post showed kindness.

literal: Later, as acting Area Commander of Jiangling, several tens of men of Shao Prefecture, Zhang Yuan and others, went to the palace gate with a memorial requesting Xi be kept.
idiomatic: Later, as acting Area Commander of Jiangling, several dozen men of Shao, led by Zhang Yuan, petitioned at the palace gate to keep Xi.

literal: The emperor sighed in admiration a long while and ordered him back to Shao; the elders congratulated one another.
idiomatic: The emperor sighed long in admiration and sent him back to Shao. The elders congratulated one another.

literal: Soon he successively served as Inspector of Luo and Xiong; he also had rough kindness in government.
idiomatic: He soon held Luo and Xiong in turn and showed a rough but genuine kindness in office.

literal: Because of illness he returned to the capital and died at home; posthumous name Jing.
idiomatic: Illness brought him back to the capital; he died at home, posthumous name Jing.

literal: He had a son Zhiben.
idiomatic: He had a son Zhiben.

literal: Xi's younger brother Quan held the posts Senior Colonel of the Third Rank, Junior Minister of Personnel, and Duke of Changshan.
idiomatic: Xi's younger brother Quan was Senior Colonel of the Third Rank, Junior Minister of Personnel, and Duke of Changshan.
